#### 5. neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis 10  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.442)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2022377, Reactome:R-HSA-6798695)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6AP2 (HGNC:782) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal acidification (GO:0005774); lysosomal acidification (GO:0005774) —DECREASES→ autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000281); autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000281) —LEADS_TO→ parkinsonism (HP:0001297); autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000281) —LEADS_TO→ spasticity (HP:0002090); autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000281) —LEADS_TO→ neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (HP:0002344). This dual impairment leads to the accumulation of toxic cellular debris and dysfunction, manifesting as parkinsonism and spasticity in X-linked parkinsonism-spasticity syndrome and neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis in NCL10.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in ATP6AP2 are found to be exclusively gain-of-function or dominant-negative in nature for either disease, or if the two diseases are shown to converge on entirely separate downstream pathways unrelated to lysosomal function. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing the specific disease-causing variants in ATP6AP2 are common (>1%) in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting lysosomal acidification or enhancing autophagy could offer therapeutic strategies for both X-linked parkinsonism-spasticity syndrome and NCL10, given their shared mechanistic basis in lysosomal dysfunction.
